pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The North Dakota Journeyman Electrician examination is part of the state electrical licensing process. Candidates preparing for this exam should follow the current North Dakota State Electrical Board application and testing instructions before scheduling. The licensing process may include application review, documentation of qualifying electrical experience or training, examination approval, and final license issuance requirements. The North Dakota Journeyman Electrician exam is designed to measure whether the candidate understands the electrical knowledge required to work as a licensed journeyman electrician. Journeyman-level testing focuses on practical trade knowledge, code application, safety, wiring methods, calculations, and the ability to apply NEC rules to real installation scenarios.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: North Dakota journeyman electrician preparation should include the National Electrical Code, electrical theory, practical installation knowledge, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, overcurrent protection, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and calculations. Candidates should also be prepared to review North Dakota-specific electrical rules and licensing responsibilities when those topics are included in the exam materials or application instructions. Electrical calculations are an important part of journeyman-level preparation. Candidates should practice service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit calculations, conductor ampacity, conductor adjustment and correction, voltage drop, box fill, raceway fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, demand factors, neutral loads, continuous loads, and overcurrent protection sizing. Calculation questions can be challenging under time pressure, so repeated practice is a key part of preparation.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The North Dakota Master Electrician examination is part of the licensing process administered by the North Dakota State Electrical Board. The examinations are based on fundamental electricity, laws, rules, the Wiring Standards of North Dakota, and the current edition of the National Electrical Code. Candidates must test within the exam window provided after receiving an exam invitation, and the passing grade is 70 percent. North Dakota recognizes multiple master electrician categories. A contracting master is responsible for adhering to North Dakota wiring laws and rules and must meet the insurance-related requirements connected to contracting activity. A master of record is responsible for electrical work performed by an entity under the requirements of the state electrical rules. A non-contracting master has the same responsibility as a journeyman electrician and must work under the supervision of a contracting master or master of record when electrical work is performed.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The North Dakota master electrician licensing process begins with confirming the correct master category. Candidates should determine whether they are pursuing a contracting master, master of record, or non-contracting master license. Each category carries different responsibilities, especially when electrical contracting, supervision, business operation, or master-of-record responsibility is involved. After identifying the correct category, candidates should document their qualifying journeyman experience. North Dakota requires master electrician applicants to have completed one year as a licensed journeyman and at least 2,000 hours working as a licensed journeyman electrician under the supervision of a contracting master electrician or master of record. Once the candidate is ready to apply, the application is submitted through the North Dakota State Electrical Board process. The Board reviews the application and determines whether the candidate is eligible to test.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: North Dakota uses a state-level electrical licensing structure. The North Dakota State Electrical Board examines applicants, issues electrical licenses, and has jurisdiction over electrical installations. Candidates pursuing a North Dakota Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path. The master electrician credential is an advanced license for experienced electrical professionals. North Dakota master applicants must have the required licensed journeyman experience and must meet the state’s supervision and work-hour requirements. Candidates should also understand the differences between contracting master, master of record, and non-contracting master categories before applying. North Dakota also regulates supervision, electrical work, and installation compliance. Electrical work must be performed under the supervision required by the applicable license category. Contracting activity may require additional responsibilities, including insurance-related requirements and compliance with state electrical rules.
